title: Curated-source identification: a GOVERNED (non-self-assignable) canonical marker + scope rules
priority_note: The resolver (31.2) trusts 'curated', so curated status must be GOVERNED (an agent cannot self-promote its own article to authoritative) — otherwise the hybrid path is poisonable. No dependencies. Enhanced-review round 1 applied.

background.reference: GitHub issues #305/#306; hub 820602df. Composes the EXISTING knowledge subsystem. Review round 1: category alone is agent-self-assignable (article.ex changeset does NOT role-gate :published/:category), so 'curated' must key off a governed signal; and system-scoped (public-wiki) articles must be handled explicitly.
background.includes: Articles have category (Categories.all(): pattern/decision/finding/reference/playbook/insight/entity/idea/quote/question), status [:draft,:published,:archived,:superseded], and scope [:tenant,:system]. There is NO curated-answer flag ('canonical' in knowledge.ex is dedup/conflict only), and hubs are NOT modeled (emergent via article_link degree). loopctl DOES have curation governance (kb_curation.ex / kb_curation_event.ex).

story.i_want_to: identify a published article as 'curated' only via a GOVERNED marker (admin/curation-gated, not an agent-settable category), define how system-scoped canonical articles participate, and expose a curated?/1 + scoped listing
story.so_that: the resolver can prefer curated answers without an agent being able to self-promote poisoned content to authoritative

rationale: The value of the hybrid interface is 'trust curated'. If curated == category in {reference,playbook,pattern} on a self-published article, any agent that writes a :reference article becomes authoritative — a direct poisoning path, since the article changeset does not gate who may publish. Basing curated on a governed marker (kb_curation) makes provenance trustworthy; category is a filter, not sufficient alone.

acceptance_criteria.description: The curated predicate is PINNED and governed: a published article is 'curated' iff it carries a governed curated marker set through an admin/curation-gated path (reuse/extend kb_curation governance), NOT merely by an agent-settable category. Category may be a filter but is never sufficient alone. If a marker column/state is added it is set only via the governed path (agents cannot self-assign it).
Loopctl.Knowledge.curated?/1 and a scoped listing return curated status, keyed on the governed marker + published status. A pure predicate is unit-testable.

System-scope handling is explicit: system-scoped (tenant_id nil, public-wiki) canonical articles MAY participate in the hybrid path as curated, but a tenant's OWN curated article takes precedence over a system one (a system canonical never overrides a tenant's fresher/own answer), and system articles never leak as another tenant's private content. The decision + precedence is documented.

Only :published articles are curated; :draft/:archived/:superseded are excluded. Additionally, an article in an OPEN :potential_conflict is NOT treated as authoritative curated without the conflict being surfaced (ties to US-31.2 AC-31.2.6).

Curated identification is tenant-scoped for tenant articles; the two-tenant isolation test runs consistently with how knowledge reads scope (explicit tenant_id predicate via AdminRepo/HeavyRead — RLS does not backstop these reads).

test_cases.name: curated? requires the governed marker, not just category
preconditions: a published :reference article WITHOUT the governed curated marker (agent-authored)
a published article WITH the governed marker
expected_results: the agent-authored reference article is NOT curated (self-promotion blocked); the governed-marked one is curated

test_cases.name: draft/superseded/conflicted are not authoritative curated
preconditions: a published governed article in an open potential_conflict
steps: curated?/1 + the authoritative check on each
expected_results: draft and superseded are not curated; the conflicted one is not returned as authoritative curated without the conflict surfaced

test_cases.name: system canonical participates but does not override a tenant's own curated
preconditions: a system-scoped curated article on topic X
tenant_a's OWN curated article on topic X
steps: resolve curated sources for tenant_a on topic X
expected_results: tenant_a's own curated article takes precedence; the system one is available but does not override; no cross-tenant private leak

test_cases.name: curated listing is tenant-isolated
preconditions: tenant_a with a governed curated article
expected_results: none of tenant_a's private curated articles appear

technical_notes: Governance: reuse kb_curation.ex / kb_curation_event.ex for the curated marker's authoring path; the marker must NOT be settable via the ordinary article changeset (article.ex does not role-gate :published).
Categories are Loopctl.Knowledge.Categories.all(); use as a filter, not the sole signal.
Hubs are NOT modeled — do not key curated on 'hub membership'. If hub enrichment is wanted, define it operationally as >= N outgoing :relates_to article_links.

System scope: @scope_values [:tenant, :system]; system articles (tenant_id nil) are served by get_system_article_by_slug/list_system_articles and are excluded from tenant search by the tenant_id predicate — AC-31.1.3 must decide their participation explicitly.
Tenant isolation is explicit-predicate on AdminRepo/HeavyRead (BYPASSRLS), not Postgres RLS (knowledge.ex header) — thread tenant_id, don't rely on RLS.
Tests use Loopctl.Fixtures.fixture/2 (fixture(:article, category:, status:, scope:)).
